title: C1 Walsh-Fourier series in L log L
detail: The best fit by far. The obstruction is identical (sup over characters of a modulated dyadic martingale at the L log L endpoint), and the decoding identity is exact for Walsh characters because the noise acts by dyadic addition. The Ginibre input becomes the GKS/Griffiths second inequality for Ising-type ferromagnets, which is classical. The Lean is already finite and dyadic (Grid M = ZMod 2^M, compression over an arbitrary finite abelian group, channel-agnostic Fisher lemmas), so a Walsh version is mostly a change of characters plus removal of the Fourier-transfer layer. It is a separate open problem. A sceptic will call it 'the same theorem in a different group', so it shows portability rather than a cross-problem eureka.

title: C3 Bourgain's multi-frequency lemma (sharp power of log N)
detail: This is the canonical place where a loss in the number of frequencies is the whole difficulty, and it feeds Bourgain's polynomial ergodic theorems. If the label plus gap-potential bookkeeping gives a frequency-count-free information cost, then the packing term log|B_A(r)| ~ log N should be the only loss, which would improve (log N)^2 towards log N. The input is in L^2 rather than a density, so the 'two-law' transfer needs an L^2 analogue. Confidence is low-medium, but this is the most informative test of whether the device is a genuine eureka beyond its own theorem.

title: C12 Variational Carleson near L^1
detail: The variation norm replaces a single frequency selector by many. The label's Fisher budget does not depend on the number of decoded frequencies, so the extension looks natural through the delayed vector estimate. The payoff is a likely new endpoint result. It sits in the same family of problems, so as evidence it is weaker than C3.

title: C2 Vilenkin bounded-type L log L
detail: The same mechanism with m-ary digits. Pinsker for m-ary digits and Ginibre for clock models are standard. This is a genuine open problem with a clear adaptation path, but it is a corollary-type extension of C1.

title: C8 Cubic partial sums on T^d in L log L
detail: Antonov's L(log L)^d endpoint looks like an artefact of iterating one-dimensional bounds. A single joint label on T^d, with one Fisher budget over 2^d-ary digits, might avoid the iteration. This is speculative: the cube partial-sum operator may not reduce to a single modulated dyadic estimate. It is a different problem, though, and the obstruction (iterated frequency-selection losses) is a reasonable match.

title: Almost-everywhere convergence of Walsh-Fourier series for f in L log L (Walsh analogue of the L log L conjecture). Best known: L log L log log log L (Sjolin-Soria / Antonov method; Di Plinio weak-L^p bounds for Walsh-Carleson).
reference: Di Plinio, 'Weak-L^p bounds for the Carleson and Walsh-Carleson operators', arXiv:1312.0398; Sjolin-Soria 2003; Oniani arXiv:2002.00350 (context)
status: open (no resolution found as of Oct 2026)
match: Exact: Walsh partial sums are modulated dyadic martingales; sup over Walsh frequencies with no loss in their number at the L log L endpoint. The paper's Prop dyadic is already a dyadic statement; the Fourier transfer step (Sec 11) is not even needed.
payoff: Resolves (a.e. Walsh-Fourier convergence in L log L, plus weak-type L log L bound for Walsh-Carleson).
confidence: medium-high that the device adapts; med…
detail: Replace the circle by the Cantor group Z_2^M (the Lean already works on Grid M = ZMod 2^M and the Compress layer over an arbitrary finite abelian group). Thermal forms A = sum_s lambda_s (1 - w_s) with Walsh characters w_s (Ising-type ferromagnetic energy); Griffiths/GKS second inequality gives Cov_{K_A}(w_u, w_v) >= 0, so cred-monotonicity, Delta_A subadditivity and F monotonicity transfer. Decoding is exact: w_n(Y xor theta) = w_n(Y) w_n(theta). Spatial forms S_p become indicator-type energies of the dyadic digits below |p|. The Fisher-sum lemmas (bit_def, space_deficit, fisher_bound) are channel-agnostic in Lean (k : Grid M -> Law alpha) and transfer verbatim.

title: A.e. convergence of Vilenkin-Fourier series on bounded-type Vilenkin groups for f in L log L. Best known: L log+L log+log+log+L (Oniani 2020).
reference: G. Oniani, 'On Sjolin-Soria-Antonov type extrapolation for locally compact groups', arXiv:2002.00350
status: open
match: Same as C1 with Z_m-adic trees (m_j bounded): maximal modulated martingale over many characters.
payoff: Resolves (L log L for bounded Vilenkin systems).
detail: Thermal forms sum lambda_s (1 - Re psi_s) on prod Z_{m_j}; positivity of Fourier coefficients of e^{-A} holds for each factor (same expansion as in the paper's proof); covariance positivity for Z_m clock models is Ginibre's inequality (valid for plane rotators and Z_N clock models). Fisher bound: replace 'bias of a fair bit' by KL of an m_j-ary digit to uniform (Pinsker) - constant depends on sup m_j, which is why bounded type is needed.

title: Sharp logarithmic loss in Bourgain's multi-frequency lemma: || sup_j | sum_{theta in Lambda} (Phi_j * (f-hat restricted near theta))^vee | ||_2 <= C (log N)^2 ||f||_2 for |Lambda| = N separated frequencies; the optimal power of log N is not known (lower bounds of fractional power only).
reference: Bourgain 1989 (IHES) Lemma 4.11; Nazarov-Oberlin-Thiele arXiv:0912.3010; Krause-Mirek-Trojan arXiv:1504.04132; Krause arXiv:2502.12887
status: open (exact exponent)
match: Strong: the loss is precisely a loss in the number of frequencies of a maximal modulated average, the obstruction the paper says the label removes ('control many modulation frequencies without a loss that grows with their number').
payoff: Possible improvement of (log N)^2 to log N (or a new proof of the known bound); not a guaranteed resolution.
detail: Model on a dyadic tree; attach a thermal label whose form is the sum of (1 - cos 2 pi theta y) over the N frequency centres (cheap updates correspond to adding a frequency to the ball). The Fisher sum is paid by the L^2 'entropy' (Gaussian/variance analogue of the chain rule, since here the input is L^2 not a density). The key question is whether the gap potential gives cost O(log N) total (packing entropy of N points) instead of O(log^2 N).

title: Konyagin's lacunary conjecture: for lacunary (n_k), S_{n_k} f -> f a.e. for every f in L log log L. Best known: L log log L log log log log L (Lie; Di Plinio); Lie 2019 proved the lacunary Carleson operator maps L log L to L^1 (sharp).
reference: Lie, arXiv:1902.03630 and arXiv:1408.4783; Di Plinio, 'Lacunary Fourier and Walsh-Fourier series near L^1', arXiv:1304.3943; Di Plinio-Lerner
status: open
match: Partial: the endpoint loss comes from tracking the selected frequency across scales; the label separates information cost from frequency-choice cost. But lacunary frequencies are ~1 per scale, so the multi-frequency obstruction is weak; the binding constraint is the budget calibration (d vs log d).
payoff: New bound at best
detail: Run the procedure with budget log d instead of d per layer: the Fisher sum is O(d) by entropy, which is too large; one would need a label whose information is charged only at the O(log d) scales where the lacunary frequency changes behaviour. Unclear.

title: Konyagin's optimal Orlicz class: between the divergence class (phi(u)=o(u sqrt(log u/log log u)), Konyagin 2000) and L log L; does a.e. convergence hold in some class strictly larger than L log L (Lie suggests L sqrt(log L) for the Lorentz C-space question)?
reference: Konyagin, ICM 2006 / Konyagin 2000; Lie, 'The pointwise convergence of Fourier series (I)', arXiv:1408.4783
status: open (gap now between L log L and the Konyagin divergence class, if 075 is correct)
match: The paper's method is calibrated to L log L: every budget is O(d) and sum m_j 2^j = int |f| log|f|. Pushing below needs an o(d) Fisher sum, i.e. a label that reveals less than the full entropy.
payoff: New bound / possible resolution of the optimal-space question
detail: Use a coarser label (tighten A only until c_A >= 1/2 on fewer frequencies) and pay the residual frequency choices by a sqrt(d) Gaussian-chaining bound; speculative.

title: Pointwise ergodic theorem along squares (n^2), polynomials or primes in L log L (or any Orlicz class between L^1 and L^p, p>1). Fails in L^1 (Buczolich-Mauldin; LaVictoire); holds in L^p, p>1 (Bourgain).
reference: Buczolich-Mauldin, 'Divergent square averages', arXiv:math/0504067; Buczolich-Eisner arXiv:1907.11060; Bourgain 1989
status: open as far as found (no source stating it closed)
match: Partial: Bourgain's L^p proof passes through the multi-frequency lemma at the rationals a/q (loss in number of frequencies) and interpolation; the label device addresses the frequency-count loss but the arithmetic (major/minor arc) structure and the L^1 counterexample constrain the endpoint.
payoff: New bound at best
detail: Transfer to Z, attach thermal labels whose forms are built from the major-arc frequencies a/q, decode each major-arc projection by integrating against a label character.

title: Bourgain's return-times theorem beyond the known range (Demeter-Lacey-Tao-Thiele: p>1, q>=2; Demeter: 1/p+1/q<3/2); fails for p=q=1 (Assani-Buczolich-Mauldin). Endpoint questions near L^1 (e.g. L log L x L log L) remain.
reference: Demeter-Lacey-Tao-Thiele, Duke 2008, arXiv:math/0601455; Demeter arXiv:0904.1254; Assani-Presser survey arXiv:1209.0856
status: open (range near the endpoint)
match: Medium: the difficulty 'is at the level of Carleson-Hunt' (survey): one needs Carleson-type control of sup over frequencies selected by the second system. A Carleson-free information-theoretic engine is exactly what is missing for endpoint cases.
payoff: Possible extension of range
detail: Use the paper's Prop dyadic (with labels) as the Carleson input for the first function, uniformly over the frequency selector; the labels need to be compatible with the second (independent) system's selector.

title: a.e. convergence of cubic (square) partial sums of multiple Fourier series on T^d for f in L log L (best known Antonov: L (log L)^d log log log L).
reference: Antonov 2004 (Izvestiya); Sjolin 1975 Ark. Mat. 14
status: open as far as found (optimal class not established)
match: Medium: cube partial sums reduce to products of one-dimensional modulated operators; the extra (log L)^{d-1} comes from iterating 1-D bounds; a joint label on T^d with a single Fisher budget could avoid iteration.
payoff: Improvement from L(log L)^d to L log L for cubes (if the reduction is not intrinsically iterative)
detail: Thermal forms on T^d (sums of 1 - cos(2 pi s.y)), positivity survives (product of one-site densities and multi-site Ginibre); dyadic cubes as the spatial tree with 2^d children (bit -> d-bit digit; Pinsker constant depends on d).

title: Polynomial Carleson operator (sup over polynomial phases of degree <= k) near L^1, e.g. L log L-type weak bound / a.e. convergence of polynomially modulated partial sums.
reference: Lie, 'The polynomial Carleson operator', arXiv:1105.4504; Zorin-Kranich
status: endpoint near L^1 open (as far as found)
match: Medium: many (polynomial) frequencies. But the decoding identity uses that linear characters factor under translation, chi_n(Y+theta)=chi_n(Y)chi_n(theta); polynomial phases do not.
payoff: New bound at best
detail: Noise would have to live on a nilmanifold/Heisenberg group (translation by theta acts on polynomial phases via a group law) with a positivity property replacing Ginibre; no such positivity theorem is known to us.

title: Nonlinear (SU(2)) Carleson conjecture / weak-L^2 bound for the nonlinear Carleson operator.
reference: Alexis-Mnatsakanyan-Thiele arXiv:2507.05124; SU(1,1) counterexample preprint arXiv:2605.25108; Poltoratski Annals 2024
status: open (SU(2)); strong SU(1,1) version reported false
match: Weak: the nonlinear partial sums are products of SU(2) matrices, not linear statistics; decoding by label characters has no analogue.
payoff: none expected
detail: None convincing.

title: Stein's conjecture for the Hilbert transform along Lipschitz vector fields beyond the short-scale L^2 bound (release family 083), and Zygmund's maximal-average conjecture; these reduce (Lacey-Li) to Carleson-type control along lines uniformly over directions.
reference: Release family 083 (A uniform Hilbert transform estimate for Lipschitz directions); Lacey-Li, Mem. AMS 2010
status: open beyond the short-scale case
match: Medium-weak: the time-frequency (Lacey-Thiele tiles) machinery used by 083 is what the label replaces in 075, but the directional geometry (Kakeya-type) is a separate obstruction the label does not touch.
payoff: Possible simplification of the 1-D Carleson input; not a resolution
detail: Replace 083's tile analysis of the one-dimensional Carleson-along-lines input by the label-based Prop dyadic; the directional maximal part remains.

title: Variational Carleson near L^1: r-variation (r>2) of partial Fourier sums for f in L log L (OSTTW proved L^p, p>1).
reference: Oberlin-Seeger-Tao-Thiele-Wright, 'A variation norm Carleson theorem', JEMS 2012
status: endpoint near L^1 open as far as found
match: Strong but 'same family': the variation norm is a sup over partitions, i.e. over many frequency families; the label budget is frequency-count-free.
payoff: Likely extension (L log L variational bound)
detail: Replace max_u by a variation over u in Prop dyadic; the delayed vector estimate (Sec 8) must control sum over jumps of label-decoded increments; the Fisher budget is unchanged.

title: Carleson's theorem (a.e. convergence of Fourier series of L^2 functions on the circle)
reference: Carleson 1966; Lean: fpvandoorn/carleson (Becker et al., arXiv:2609.31334; blueprint arXiv:2405.06423, 130 pp)
match: Lean carleson repo ~2.41 MB of Lean (GitHub language stats; proves a generalisation on doubling metric measure spaces); blueprint 130 pages. The 075 Lean (no Carleson import) proves the stronger L log L statement in 1.28 MB / 29.2k lines, of which ~10k lines (53/155 files) touch the label channel/F…
payoff: Add Thermal.label/channel + fisher_bound + duet_decode to L; ask a prover for the L^2 a.e. statement on AddCircle via a GridBound-type route; compare against the budget needed with only Mathlib + Carleson's original tools. Confounded by the rest of the 075 cluster (compression lemma).

title: Walsh-Carleson theorem (Billard 1967: a.e. convergence of Walsh-Fourier series for L^2; Sjolin: L^p)
reference: Billard 1967; Sjolin 1969; Thiele, 'Wave packet analysis' (CBMS 105, 2006) Walsh model chapters
match: ~20-30 pages for the Walsh model via Lacey-Thiele tiles (Thiele's notes); no Lean formalization known
payoff: Formalise on ZMod 2^M with Walsh characters; with the label device (Ising-type forms) the proof should reduce to the Dyadic+Thermal+Procedure layers without the Fourier transfer. Clean measurement of the device on its home turf.

title: Bourgain's multi-frequency lemma (log^2 N loss) in a finite/dyadic model
reference: Bourgain 1989 IHES Lemma 4.11; Nazarov-Oberlin-Thiele arXiv:0912.3010
match: ~8-12 pages (Bourgain's proof via Rademacher-Menshov chaining + Littlewood-Paley); not formalised
payoff: Does adding the label device let a prover obtain the bound (or log N) faster? This is the cleanest 'frequency-count-free' test.

title: Kolmogorov-Seliverstov-Plessner theorem: Fourier series converge a.e. if sum |c_n|^2 log n < infinity
reference: Kolmogorov-Seliverstov 1925, Plessner 1926; Zygmund, Trigonometric Series Vol. I, Ch. XIII
match: ~3-4 pages classical (dyadic chaining)
payoff: Positive-direction sanity check: with labels the log n loss should disappear entirely (it is subsumed by Carleson), so the test measures whether a prover finds the label route at all; short classical proof makes the speedup ratio small.

title: Scalar entropy bound for the dyadic Fisher/square function: sum_I |I| (<rho>_{I+} - <rho>_{I-})^2 / <rho>_I <= C int rho log(rho/<rho>) (the label-free special case A = 0)
reference: folklore (chain rule + Pinsker); Bellman-function literature on dyadic Carleson embeddings
match: ~1 page on paper; Lean: special case of bit_def/space_deficit with k = no_label (Procedure/Fisher.lean:51)
payoff: Control: the device should give NO speedup here (A=0 is the trivial channel); confirms the measurement is not just rewarding the entropy chain rule.

title: Rademacher-Menshov theorem (a.e. convergence of orthogonal series with sum |a_n|^2 log^2 n < infinity; sharp for general ONS)
reference: Rademacher 1922, Menshov 1923
match: ~3 pages
payoff: Negative control: the loss is sharp for general orthonormal systems with no translation structure, so a shift-invariant positive-definite label cannot help; a 'speedup' here would indicate a flawed evaluation.

title: C1 contracting-on-average self-similar measures on R (separation-free)
detail: This is the structurally closest setting to 148. It is one-dimensional and the slopes commute, so block types still fix the signed contraction and the typed block laws are finite real laws to which the pair bound applies verbatim. The only new work is stopping-time blocks (for expanding maps), uniform nonsaturation for the contracting-on-average stationary measure, and window bookkeeping. The current literature (Kittle-Kogler 2501.17795) needs an all-scales weak separation, so this would be a genuine new theorem. However, the Kittle-Kogler variance energy is a ready-made competitor, so c_ell is unlikely to be the decisive device.

title: C9 countably infinite IFS on R
detail: Pair capacity is defined for finite laws. Truncating the IFS gives finite typed block laws at a controlled entropy cost, and the sumset bound only needs k to be chosen after the truncation. The transfer is likely routine given 148, which makes it a good test of whether the device transfers with little extra budget. It is also weak evidence of eureka value, because the transfer stays within the same problem family.

title: C3 random / non-autonomous self-similar measures
detail: 148 already imports the GSSY random-IFS type machinery. In a random environment the typed block law is still a finite law, and the Jensen-over-future step becomes Jensen over the environment. Expected payoff: quenched separation-free dimension formulas. Medium confidence, medium difficulty; again an extension within the same family.

title: C2 R^d with commuting linear parts (separation-free Hochman trichotomy)
detail: The pair bound generalises with capacities c_{ell,theta} over annulus bands and direction sectors. The genuinely new issue is directional nonsaturation (Hochman saturation), which naturally produces the third alternative of the trichotomy. Kittle-Kogler claim their method extends to virtually solvable rotation groups (including d=2), so the payoff is an independent proof rather than a first resolution. High difficulty.

title: C4 real-analytic self-conformal IFS on R
detail: The hidden-fine-scale-entropy obstruction is identical, and the pair bound applies to finite position laws. The obstacle is that derivative types do not identify composed maps up to translation (P22 fails), so c_ell would carry only half the argument. Low-medium confidence. It is worth listing because Rapaport and Kaenmaki (2024-2026) leave exactly the ESC-free case open.

title: Entropy-rate (generalised exact-overlaps) dimension formula for contracting-on-average self-similar measures on R: dim nu = min{1, h_RW/|chi|}. Here mu is finitely supported on Sim(R), contracting on average (its support may contain expanding maps), and no separation is assumed.
reference: Kittle-Kogler, Dimension of contracting on average self-similar measures, arXiv:2501.17795 (2025); companion paper arXiv:2409.18936
status: Partially solved. It is proved under M_n >= e^{-cn} for infinitely many n, and under the weak all-scales condition log …
match: Exact match on the hidden-fine-scale-entropy side. Block laws of stopped random walks are finite real laws that can condense arbitrarily. The pair bound is a statement about a single finite law, so it does not matter whether the maps contract.
payoff: Would prove the separation-free formula in this setting (a new theorem), or give an alternative to Kittle-Kogler variance summation.
detail: Replace fixed-length n-blocks by stopping-time blocks: stop when |product of slopes| first drops below 2^{-An}. Slopes in Sim(R) commute, so block types (letter counts) still fix the signed slope product. Apply the pair bound to each typed block law to get expected sum_ell c_ell >= c n in a finite band. Redeem this through the two-point gain against the stationary measure, which is still nonsaturated because d<1. The separated-band count is unchanged. New inputs needed: uniform nonsaturation (P12), and the Feng-Hu-type upper bound and exact dimensionality for contracting-on-average stationary measures (exact dimensionality is known in this setting, cf. Kittle-Kogler).

title: Exact-overlaps / entropy-rate dimension formula for self-similar measures in R^d whose linear parts commute (e.g. scalar contractions r_i I, or a common rotation). Claim: dim mu = min{d, h_RW/chi} unless mu saturates along an invariant subspace. This is the Hochman trichotomy without the super-exponential-condensation alternative.
reference: Hochman, On self-similar sets with overlaps and inverse theorems for entropy in R^d, arXiv:1503.09043 (Memoirs AMS); Kittle-Kogler arXiv:2610.10511 Sec. 1 (claims the method extends when the rotation parts generate a virtually solvable group)
status: Open in the literature before Oct 2026: Hochman requires exponential separation, and in R^d the conjecture must include…
match: Pair-bound side: the k-fold-sum observation and random nested grids work in R^d with cubes, and the capacity becomes a packing over annulus bands. Gain side: the two-point gain needs mu to be nonsaturated in the DIRECTION of the pair. That is exactly Hochman saturation, and it is the new difficulty.
payoff: A new proof of a separation-free R^d trichotomy in the commuting case, and a first one there if Kittle-Kogler do not write theirs out. It would also give the planar case independently of Kittle-Kogler.
detail: Define c_{ell,theta}(nu) using bands of |x-y| AND direction sectors theta, from a finite cover of the sphere. Pair bound: run the randomised partition with cubes. The cost per level is controlled by the mean |x-y| within cells, which splits into direction sectors, giving k(H - H_rho) <= log|kF| + C_{k,d} sum_{ell,theta} c_{ell,theta}. Gain: if mu is not saturated on lines in direction theta, the directional analogue of Delta_v is uniformly positive and the two-point gain carries over. If mu is saturated on an invariant subspace, we are in the third alternative of the trichotomy. Block types fix the (commuting) linear part, so P22 survives.

title: Dimension of random, non-autonomous or inhomogeneous self-similar measures on R without exponential separation: a.s. dim = min{1, (map entropy rate)/chi}. Examples: random Bernoulli convolutions, the Galicer-Saglietti-Shmerkin-Yavicoli random IFS, and the Saglietti-Shmerkin-Solomyak non-homogeneous families.
reference: Galicer-Saglietti-Shmerkin-Yavicoli, L^q dimensions and projections of random measures, Nonlinearity 2016 (arXiv:1504.04893); Saglietti-Shmerkin-Solomyak, Adv. Math. 2018 (arXiv:1709.05092)
status: Known results use transversality or separation, or hold only for almost every parameter. A separation-free formula for …
match: The 148 proof already uses the GSSY block-type disintegration, and the random environment is exactly where the types machinery originated. The obstruction is the same: hidden fine-scale entropy in the typed block laws.
payoff: New theorems: quenched separation-free dimension formulas for random self-similar families. Medium novelty.
detail: Condition on the environment. The typed block law nu_{omega,n} is again a finite law with fixed slope, so the pair bound applies. The Jensen-over-future-types step (P27) becomes Jensen over the future environment. This requires the environment to be stationary and ergodic, so that the averaged tail is a scaled copy of a fixed nonsaturated measure. The pair capacity needs no change.

title: Exact-overlaps analogue for self-conformal measures of real-analytic IFS on R: dimension = min{1, h_RW/chi}, assuming only that composed maps have no exact overlaps.
reference: Rapaport, Dimension of self-conformal measures associated to an exponentially separated analytic IFS on R, arXiv:2412.16753; holomorphic version arXiv:2608.17137; Kaenmaki, Exponential separation of self-conformal systems, arXiv:2609.23743 (Sept 2026)
status: Open without exponential separation. Rapaport proves the formula under ESC; Kaenmaki 2026 proves ESC is C^2-generic, bu…
match: Hidden fine-scale entropy among composed analytic maps, with the same Baker-type condensation possible. The pair bound applies verbatim to finite laws of positions.
payoff: Possibly a resolution of the analytic exact-overlaps conjecture on R. A partial result is more likely, e.g. for systems where the derivative type is rigid.
detail: Linearise at the relevant scale. Typed blocks fix derivatives only up to bounded distortion, so the block law is an almost-affine image. Apply the pair bound to the finite law of block positions. The two-point gain then needs a distortion-robust form, in which the pair distance is known only within a factor 1+o(1); the window margin 5/M already absorbs this. Main gap: there is no analogue of "types identify the complete composed map" (P22), because analytic maps of equal derivative type need not be translates of each other.

title: Dimension of projections of shift-invariant ergodic (Gibbs or Markov) measures onto self-similar sets with overlaps, without separation: dim pi m = min{1, h_RW(m)/chi(m)}, with the map-entropy rate in place of h(m).
reference: Jordan-Rapaport, Dimension of ergodic measures projected onto self-similar sets with overlaps, Proc. LMS 2021 (arXiv:1908.00271); universal version arXiv:2412.03529
status: Proved under exponential separation; the separation-free version is open.
match: Same hidden-entropy obstruction; the pair bound applies to the finite conditional block laws.
payoff: A new theorem for Markov and Gibbs measures. The general ergodic case is unlikely.
detail: For Markov measures, replace Bernoulli block types by Markov types (transition counts). The conditional block laws are then finite laws with fixed slope. Nonsaturation of the projected measure and the Jensen-over-future step both need the future to be conditionally independent given the boundary state, i.e. the Markov property.

title: Furstenberg (stationary) measures of a finitely supported mu on SL_2(R): dim nu_F = min{1, h_RW/(2 chi)}, without exponential separation or Diophantine hypotheses.
reference: Hochman-Solomyak, Invent. Math. 2017 (arXiv:1610.02641); Kittle, Absolutely continuous Furstenberg measures (arXiv:2305.05757); Rapaport-Ren arXiv:2511.00729
status: Open in general. Hochman-Solomyak need exponential separation; without it they obtain the formula only with h_F, the Fu…
match: Partial: fine-scale entropy of finite laws of group elements acting on P^1. The pair bound for the finite law of image points is fine; the gain side needs a local linearisation of the projective action.
payoff: Would resolve a well-known problem, but the pair capacity is not the bottleneck.
detail: In a non-abelian group, types (letter counts) do NOT fix the products, so the "types identify the composed map" step (P22) fails. One would need a different conditioning that fixes the derivative cocycles. Kittle-Kogler 2610.10511 explicitly name non-abelian addition as the obstruction for their analogue.

title: Planar self-affine measures with overlaps: dimension = Lyapunov dimension (or its entropy-rate analogue), without exponential separation.
reference: Hochman-Rapaport, Hausdorff dimension of planar self-affine sets and measures with overlaps, JEMS 2022 (arXiv:1904.09812); Barany-Hochman-Rapaport Invent. 2019
status: Open without ESC.
match: The 1-D step of the self-affine argument (entropy growth of projections convolved with fibre measures) suffers from the same hidden-fine-scale-entropy problem.
payoff: Partial only (diagonal or triangular commuting cases).
detail: Apply the pair bound to the finite laws of projected cylinder positions in a fixed Furstenberg direction, and redeem through the two-point gain against the projected measure. Non-commuting linear parts again break the type conditioning.

title: Separation-free L^q-dimension formula for self-similar measures on R: D(mu,q) equals the minimum of 1 and the similarity value from tau_q, assuming only no exact overlaps. Shmerkin proves it under ESC.
reference: Shmerkin, Annals 2019 (arXiv:1609.07802); survey arXiv:1907.07121
status: Open without exponential separation.
match: The same separation obstruction, but in L^q rather than Shannon entropy.
payoff: Would be significant, but there is no clear adaptation path.
detail: Would need an L^q pair bound. The proof of the pair bound uses the Shannon chain rule (conditioning on Y and on the cell flags), which has no Renyi analogue. A capacity for collision-type norms is conceivable but unclear.

title: Self-similar measures generated by countably many similarities on R with finite entropy: dim = min{1, h_RW/chi}, without separation.
reference: Status per the Varju survey arXiv:2509.22042, which covers finite IFS only
status: Open; the finite-IFS case is now claimed by 148 and by Kittle-Kogler.
match: Hidden fine-scale entropy as in 148, plus a tail.
payoff: A new theorem, though mostly routine given the finite case.

detail: Take the explicit constant c0 = (delta^2/L^2 - 4/D)/(4(1-1/D)) for S = {h_{I,J}}. Bound the word length of each transport in {x0,x1}: tree-pair diagrams with O(D) carets, since the intervals have depth <= 4D, and word length is comparable to the caret count (Burillo-Cleary-Stein / Fordham). This gives a Folner constant for {x0,x1} of at least c0/max|h| ~ delta^4/(C L^4), which is polynomial in 1/L and not tower-type. Then apply Cheeger/Dodziuk-Mohar to get ||x0+x0^-1+x1+x1^-1|| <= 4 - c*(Folner)^2, and Kesten/Grigorchuk to get a cogrowth bound. L comes from Lean's Analytic.displacementLipschitzConstant. The bound improves directly if one can construct B-S maps with a better L/delta ratio (optimal Lipschitz-retraction constants on Hilbert space, known only roughly: 4.5 < k0 < ~29).

New zero-free regions (complex anisotropy, inhomogeneous fields) would feed Barvinok-type algorithms (HMS 2019). The weakness is that this direction is close to the Asano/Suzuki-Fisher precedent, so success says little about novelty.

title: Negative dependence for exclusion and card shuffles (Liggett's inequality, BBL Thm 5.2 from deterministic starts, S_k shuffle SR)

The caveat is that the speedup comes from the UNSPLICED half, which is the Borcea-Branden symbol, so a positive speedup result would credit the precedent, not the eureka step. match: Exactly the same: no reflection positivity, theta = 2 loop weight, and need for negative dependence of loop-hitting events. Loops now carry crosses (prob u) and double bars (prob 1-u); double bars make loops non-orientable, so the next-pin map is a Brauer pairing, not a permutation.

detail: Replace F_pi by the Brauer symbol prod_{pairs {a,b}} (z_a + z_b) over the pairing of the 2n endpoints of a layer. A double bar on strands i,j acts on the output variables by Q: A + B y_i + C y_j + D y_i y_j -> (B + C)(y_i + y_j). I checked (this analysis) that the two-strand mixture symbol (1-u-v)(y1+w1)(y2+w2) + u(y2+w1)(y1+w2) + v(w1+w2)(y1+y2) is a homogeneous quadratic with Gram eigenvalues {2, -2u, -2v, -2(1-u-v)} (times 1/2), hence Lorentzian, hence real stable for ALL u,v >= 0, u+v <= 1; by the Borcea-Branden symbol theorem the step preserves stability, and random 3-strand Brauer laws tested numerically are stable. Splicing still gives factor 2 per closed loop. So the stability half of the device transfers to the whole XXZ family. Missing piece: output extraction. For pairings, the event 'T-endpoints are matched among themselves' is not a subset-presence event; one needs a new extraction (e.g. lowest-degree homogeneous part in T variables, which is stable and isolates exactly the configurations with no E-T pairs) and a pairing analogue of the presence inequality. The rest of the OAI proof (hole walks, return energy, Nash/flows) would also need an easy-plane version.

title: C1: generalized Hilbert–Smith for ENR Z-homology manifolds
detail: This is the only candidate where the device itself, not just the theorem, does the new work. Yang's theorem shows homology manifolds carry exactly the same wild-orbit-space obstruction. Every ingredient of z_i has a homology-manifold analogue: Verdier duality with orientation sheaf, Newman via Smith theory, and the A_t in T(X) membership via the ENR-retract summand trick, which works precisely because T is generated by arbitrary continuous maps and closed under summands. The open step is replacing the S^d -> W^+ collapse by a compact ENR source and checking the degree-one identity. The caveat is Mj's remark that a topological analogue fails 'on homology manifolds'. The cited Raymond–Williams spaces are 2-dimensional compacta, so the remark probably does not apply, but it must be checked first. A success would be strong evidence for a confirmed eureka step.

title: C2: Mj's QI-group / pattern-rigidity theorems without the Hausdorff-dimension hypothesis
detail: Mj's dim_Haus < dim_t + 2 hypothesis exists only because his integral obstruction is a Hausdorff-dimension count (Repovš–Ščepin/Martin style). Character classes are metric-free, so on boundaries of PD hyperbolic groups (Z-homology manifolds) they would remove it. That would give unconditional Lie-ness of finite-dimensional locally compact QI groups and stronger pattern rigidity. This depends on C1 plus ANR-type regularity of ∂G. For S^2 boundaries (Cannon setting, family 246) the 304 theorem applies directly.

title: C3: local (pseudogroup) Hilbert–Smith

It is cheap and likely correct, but may be a routine corollary rather than a recognised open problem, and that status is unverified.
